extra.message: User input from 'username' is concatenated directly into a SQL query string and executed via cur.execute() without parameterized queries, resulting in SQL Injection.
User-controlled filename is passed directly to the open() function without any sanitization or validation, allowing an attacker to read arbitrary files via path traversal.

The fetchimage function accepts an unsanitized URL from user input and retrieves its contents using requests.get() without validating the destination host or protocol, leading to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).
The input 'mathexp' is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered, resulting in Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) which can lead to Remote Code Execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Template Directives Using a Template Engine
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: User input from the 'username' parameter in the POST body is directly reflected in the JSON response without sanitization or output encoding. Under certain configurations, this can lead to reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

The 'Host' header of the incoming HTTP request is extracted and reflected directly into the response without any validation or sanitization, making the application vulnerable to HTTP Header Injection and host-header-based attacks.
